x: As it turned out Ray had to contend with Bob Dobson who walked an inspired race to win by just 60 seconds from Ray who was fast catching him over the last lap.

With a superb display of speed Wilf Wesch beat 50 Minutes and Bob Dobson by just 1 second. Barry Ingarfield was disqualified and although McMullen deputised to good effect we were not up to the strength of Basildon in the team.

Carl was overtaken by Bob Dobson in the closing stages but hung on to beat 4 hours 20 minutes and gain selection for the European Games. Ray Middleton headed the second group but his fifth position was not up to the high standards he has set himself in recent years.
Ray Middleton proved not quite good enough to catch Bob Dobson and Len Duquemin and John Moullin walked their usual races in this event to finish in the first fifteen.

This race with a Belgrave match in conjunction was won by Bob Dobson in a rather fast time of 50:23mins. Belgrave's first man home was 3rd placed Carl Lawton, three minutes down on Dobson and just clear of Lord of Highgate.
National Police match at Henlow on Thursday 5th April, Ray Middleton, 85:30, finished second to Bob Dobson, 83:41.
In the Essex 20 mile race held on April 21st, John Moullin finished 3rd in 2hrs 45m 40 secs. Bob Dobson was the winner.

By 15 km the leading group had split and was left with Roger Mills, Jake Warhurst and Bob Dobson contesting. The Bels retained their dominance although the positions had changed to Len, Carl, John, Allan and Ray.
John Moullin (4:28:08) finished second to Bob Dobson of Basildon (4:24:52) in a 50 kilometre race at Dunkirk on May 20th - a personal best.

Higher up the field Carl Lawton finished 3rd to Bob Dobson with John Bromley almost catching International John Webb. The two other Dunsfords were Babbette and Mrs. in the Girls and Ladies races respectively.
Ray Middleton was placed second in the Southern Area 50km event at Basildon on June 21st. He recorded 4:50:15 behind Bob Dobson's 4:42.
Held on a 4½ mile course in the late afternoon, the earlier part of the day being spent time-wasting, an uneventful race progressed with Bob Dobson (Southend) being the eventual winner.
Bob Dobson of the Civil Service went straight into the lead in this two lap race but at the halfway mark was only two seconds up on Carl Lawton.

The main event, the 7 miles saw the Mexican E.Vera in action, for two of the three laps he led Bob Dobson (Southend), but on the third lap he was away on his own to finish in 48:44 with Dobson second.

The 55th Open Seven promoted by Enfield was won by 50kms specialist Bob Dobson followed by Carl with John Hall not far behind. However, a rush of Steyning vests gave them first team honours, with Mike and John Newnham completing the team for second spot.

At Havering AC's track meeting on November 26th Bob Dobson (Ilford) got the better of Carl Lawton over 10 kilometres with 44:16 to 45:49. Tenth was John Newnham, 48:50, and 13th Richard Dorman, 50:24 to give the Bels first team place.

Charlie Weston (Highgate), Ed Shillabeer (Dawlish) and Bob Dobson (Southend) were the early leaders. As the hours progressed Ed Shillabeer went into a lead to win and retire at 100kms with a new British record.
